solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A consequence of abandoning Ulster

indicators.note: abandoning suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters of the province's name are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A political outcome that follows from giving up Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' reads as giving up the province, but it is the anagram signal in the sense of 'with abandon'. Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is a synonym for a consequence: what follows from some cause.

clue.text: Reminiscent of Lowell's last poem about residing in Split

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so the reversed pair goes within the split

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pair is read backwards
last picks the final letter of the poet's name

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Robert Lowell's final poem looks back on living in the Croatian city of Split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as the Croatian city, but it is a tear. 'about' turns the poet's last letter and the poem round to EDOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent of something means strongly suggestive or evocative of it.

clue.text: No cover charge here?

parts.note: a cover charge is an entry fee; here the performers literally charge for no cover, taking their clothes off

explanation.surface: A nightclub-goer asks whether there is no entry fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' reads as a door fee, but the venue is one where nothing stays covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancers at this kind of venue undress, so the show offers no cover at all.

clue.text: Offering little hope bishop rejected disclosure of secret information

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so the cleric's letter is dropped

parts.note: bleak means offering little hope
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop gloomily refuses a whistleblower's revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: An unauthorised release of confidential facts to the press is a leak.

clue.text: It's said erroneously about having a love of cruelty

indicators.note: something said erroneously is put wrongly, so the letters of the phrase before it are put into a new order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A remark about something is misreported as being about a fondness for cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erroneously' rearranges ITSSAID, and C (circa) is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in inflicting pain is described by this adjective, named after the Marquis de Sade.

clue.text: Chiefly coming from a lovable rogue

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means behaving erratically, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: Something said principally by a charming scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovable rogue' is a stock phrase, but 'rogue' is the anagram signal on A LOVABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Above all means most importantly, a synonym for chiefly.

clue.text: Working to conceal French breach of agreement

indicators.note: to conceal means to hide inside, so the abbreviation goes within

parts.note: in action means working, operating

explanation.surface: A French breach of a treaty is covered up while things carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a violation or breaking of a rule or agreement.

clue.text: Fool putting away seconds gets wind

indicators.note: putting away means eating, taking in, so the fool swallows the letter

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool who gobbles second helpings ends up with flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like the noun, gas in the stomach; it is the verb pronounced to rhyme with 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist is to wind or coil something round.

clue.text: An opinion expressed by many people about her virginity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cry goes round the pronoun

parts.words: An opinion expressed by many people
parts.note: a cry, as in a popular cry, is a view loudly shared by many

explanation.surface: Many people voice a view on a woman's chastity.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is slang for virginity, as in losing one's cherry.

clue.text: Absolute crackpot's name removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so the abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: a nutter is slang for a crackpot

explanation.surface: An outright eccentric has had his name struck off.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means complete or total, as in utter nonsense, so it is a synonym of absolute.

clue.text: Sleeping with party worker Trump oddly ignored earlier

indicators.note: earlier places the kept letters of the name before the worker in the answer

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters ignored, only the second and fourth letters of the name remain

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's usual worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: A political party worker sleeps while Trump is pointedly overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' drops the first, third and fifth letters of the name, and 'earlier' fixes where the kept pair goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inactive or at rest, like a volcano or a seed, is described as sleeping.

clue.text: Away team's players try to avoid being here

definitions.text: players try to avoid being here

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
a side is a team; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: The visiting team's players are careful not to stray into a forbidden position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away team' looks like the visitors. In football an attacker is penalised for being in this position.
explanation.definitionFit: Footballers try to stay level with the last defender so as not to be caught in this illegal position.

clue.text: Language lab's earliest computer program

indicators.note: the earliest letter of the word is its first one

parts.note: an app is a computer program, short for application

explanation.surface: A language laboratory's very first computer program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language lab' looks like one phrase, but 'Language' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sami is the language of the people of northern Scandinavia, traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Supporter's complaint involves Newcastle's top player

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: involves means takes inside, so the complaint wraps round the letter

parts.note: a beef is slang for a complaint

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an actor is a player on the stage

explanation.surface: A football fan grumbles about Newcastle's star player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' puts N (Newcastle's top) inside BEEF, giving BENEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron who gives money or help is a supporter.

clue.text: The standard by which to judge a witty fool say

definitions.text: The standard by which to judge
definitions.meaning: a benchmark or criterion against which other things are tested, from the stone used to test gold
the clown in Shakespeare's As You Like It, an example of a witty fool

explanation.surface: A clever jester sets the yardstick for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark stone once tested gold, and Shakespeare named his clever clown in As You Like It after it.

clue.text: Hold with Deneuve's refusal to embrace South African golfer

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside, so the refusal goes round the golfer

parts.note: Catherine Deneuve is French, and French for no is non
Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: An actress refuses to hug a famous golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Deneuve is a French film star, so her refusal is the French NON.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling hold in which the arms are locked behind an opponent's neck goes by this name.

clue.text: That which is disclosed after vicar leaves in high spirits

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the clergyman's title goes out of the longer word

parts.note: a revelation is something disclosed
Rev is the short title of a vicar, the Reverend

explanation.surface: Something comes to light once the vicar has gone, and spirits rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness, the same as being in high spirits.

clue.text: Working to locate boxing article without delay

parts.note: on means working, functioning
the is the definite article
to spot is to locate or pick out

explanation.surface: A detective is working to track down a boxing story right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport; it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something there and then, immediately, is doing it at once.

clue.text: Mistaking danger to ancient city's magnificence

indicators.note: mistaking means getting wrong, so the letters of the hazard are put in another order

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, birthplace of Abraham

explanation.surface: Misjudging the threat to an ancient city's splendour.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour or impressiveness, a synonym of magnificence.

clue.text: Exhausted by unproductive strike

parts.note: dead means unproductive, as in a dead loss
to beat is to strike

explanation.surface: Workers worn out by a fruitless industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; it is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead beat is an informal way of saying completely worn out, exhausted.

clue.text: Posts Jack neglected to repair are unimportant

indicators.note: neglected means left out, so the card is dropped from the word

parts.note: posts are jobs, positions of employment
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
to cure is to put right or repair

explanation.surface: Fence posts left unrepaired by Jack are of no consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posts' looks like fence posts; here it means JOBS, from which J (jack) is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obscure is little known and so of little significance.

clue.text: Sally's kind to Danielle essentially

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type

indicators.note: essentially means at its heart, so the central letters of the name are taken

explanation.surface: Sally is a kindly friend to Danielle, at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name, but it is the military sense: a charge out of a besieged position.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie and a sally are both a sudden attack made by troops breaking out from a defensive position.

clue.text: Silence surrounding mountain climbing tragedies at last featured in sensational news story

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so the call for quiet encloses the rest

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upwards, so the mountain is turned backwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hushed-up mountaineering disaster ends up on the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means reading upwards, so the mountain is turned round to PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a front-page story given big, eye-catching treatment by a newspaper.

clue.text: Tidiness of fringe's first to go

indicators.note: first to go means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a border is a fringe or edge

explanation.surface: A neatly trimmed fringe is the first thing to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringe' suggests a haircut; here it is an edging, BORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Order means neatness, the state of things being arranged in their proper places.

clue.text: Worker taken in by injured player's jocularity

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the worker goes within the jumbled letters
injured means damaged, so the letters of the sportsman are knocked out of order

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An employee is fooled by a footballer who has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' scrambles the footballer's letters, apostrophe-s included, into PLEASRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A joking or good-humoured remark is a pleasantry, an act of jocularity.

clue.text: Tests showing former partner has a debilitating disease

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
MS is multiple sclerosis, a debilitating disease

explanation.surface: Medical tests show an ex-partner has a serious illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal tests of knowledge or skill.

clue.text: Minister to stop Tory leader at the start

indicators.note: at the start places the leading letter before the rest
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to end something is to stop it

explanation.surface: A government minister moves to halt the Conservative leader early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a government noun but is the verb: to minister to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after someone who is ill is to minister to their needs.

clue.text: Contributing to Romola testifying recently

indicators.note: Contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Romola has just given evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean lately, in the recent past, as in 'of late'.

clue.text: Without anyone else to carry a couple of barrels of shellfish for instance

indicators.note: to carry means to hold within, so the outer word takes in the others

parts.note: alone means without anyone else

indicators.note: a couple of means two, so the opening pair of letters of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone single-handedly lugs a pair of barrels of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of barrels' looks like two casks, but it means the word's first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible sea snail, also called ormer or paua, is one example of shellfish.

clue.text: Without having enough of a warning

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
ample means plentiful, having enough

explanation.surface: Someone lacks sufficient warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Punishing someone to deter others is making an example of them, a warning to the rest.

clue.text: Pub landlord gets to see Skinner's finally introduced

parts.note: a landlord is the host at an inn

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the letter is put inside the see

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat or see of a bishop

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A pub landlord gets to meet Skinner at last when introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's see is his diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old-fashioned or jocular word for an inn or pub.

clue.text: Leave biretta off after king departs

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the remaining letters are jumbled
departs means goes away, so the royal letter leaves the hat

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A priest is told to take his biretta off once the king has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: A biretta is a priest's square cap. 'departs' removes R (Rex) from it, and 'off' rearranges BIETTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for go away, an order to leave.
